# Shared brief: michi multi-section envelope (read fully before starting)

Repo: /Users/gabe/Projects/michi (Rust workspace; crate `michi-core` is where this lands). You work in your own git worktree.
Source of truth: `docs/spec/07-wisp-and-monokl-envelope.md` (read it). **This design is approved for implementation** by the
owner (2026-11-15). Do not re-litigate `PRINCIPLES.md` gate 3 or ADR 9's "stays a proposal" line; a later step records that
decision. Follow the rest of `AGENTS.md` and `PRINCIPLES.md` (non-negotiables: no `unwrap`/`expect` in lib code, every `pub`
item documented, `String::with_capacity`, `BTreeMap` for output maps, char-boundary truncation, tests via `cargo nextest`).

## Flow (autonomous: do not ask questions; decide, and report the decision)
1. `git fetch origin && git checkout -B <your-branch> origin/main` (branch name is in your task).
2. TDD: failing test first (confirm it fails for the right reason), then implement, then green.
3. Mutant check: for each behavioral claim, break the code on purpose, watch the test fail, revert. Report which mutants you ran.
4. Docs: `docs/spec/03-rust-api.md` gets a new subsection for your API (CI's "Spec first" job needs a docs touch for public API
   changes). Keep edits to your own subsection so parallel branches merge cleanly. Do not edit `docs/spec/06-decisions.md`,
   the ADRs or `docs/spec/README.md`: report deviations from spec 07 in your final message and PR body instead; the
   integrator consolidates them.
5. Changeset: add one `.changeset/<slug>.md` in the format the existing ones use (look at `git log -5 --stat -- .changeset`,
   `CONTRIBUTING.md` and the Callisto docs). Package `michi-core`; the fixed group releases everything together.
   Start a paragraph with `Breaking:` if rendered output of existing calls changes.
6. Checks, judged by exit code only (never by reading output): `just fmt-check`, `just clippy`, `just test-rust`,
   `just typos`, and `just semver` if it exists. Report which you ran and which you did not.
7. Commit (conventional message, why-not-what). **No claude.ai session links, no `Claude-Session` trailer.** Push the branch
   and open a **draft** PR against main with a short plain body (what, why, checked, not run). Never merge, never force-push,
   never push to main.

## Sandbox notes
Bash runs in a sandbox. Cargo (registry cache writes), `git commit` (a pre-commit hook), and `git push` need
`dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` on that one command. Use `$TMPDIR` for temp files, not `/tmp`. Prefix shell commands
with `rtk` if the hook does not already. Keep commands simple (no `$(...)`-computed git arguments).

## Shared decisions (so parallel branches agree)
- New modules: `section.rs` (slice A), `budget.rs` and `provenance.rs` (slice B). Re-export from `lib.rs` with explicit
  `pub use` lists (no globs). Touch `lib.rs` only for your own module and re-exports.
- **`returned_count` is derived, not trusted**, for `Toon` and `Kv` bodies: compute it from `rows.len()` / `items.len()`;
  there is no `debug_assert!` and no clamp, so debug and release agree. `Text` bodies take a caller-declared count.
- camelCase for every JSON key and for TOON key names in `budget:` / `provenance:` blocks (`tokensUsed`, `returnedCount`).
- Render order for a response: sections in insertion order, then `budget:`, then `provenance:`, then `help[]`, then `recovery[]`.
- Render functions always succeed; they never panic.
- JSON stays hand-built and `serde_json`-free in the default build (reuse the existing JSON string escaping helper in
  `response.rs`); `serde`/`schemars` derives only behind the existing features.

PR URL and branch; decisions that deviate from spec 07 or fill a gap in it; checks run with exit codes; mutants run;

`truncation(&outcome, guidance)` sets the count and the cut hint in one call, so `totalCount` and `help[]` always describe the same cut. It does not touch the rows: `AgentResponse` holds TOON `Value` rows, not the caller's `T`, so pass `outcome.kept` (converted) to `.items(...)`. A later `.total_count()` or `.hints()` still overrides it.

`total_count` applies to both paths. On the KV path with no items the body is just `totalCount: N` (the free `render_kv` still returns `""` for empty items), so a count the caller set is never dropped; with neither items nor a count the body is empty.

### Budget and provenance types (`budget`, `provenance`)

Plain data types for the envelope in [07-wisp-and-monokl-envelope.md](07-wisp-and-monokl-envelope.md) §2 and §3. All four are `#[non_exhaustive]`, derive `Debug`, `Clone`, `Default` (where it makes sense), `PartialEq` and `Eq`, and have builder methods. Behind `serde` they derive `Serialize` with camelCase keys (absent `Option`s skipped); behind `schemars` they derive `JsonSchema`.

- `BudgetSummary`: optional `max_tokens`, `max_bytes`, `max_items`, `tokens_used`, `bytes_used`; `truncated: bool`; `sections: Vec<SectionCost>`. Builders: `new`, `max_tokens`, `max_bytes`, `max_items`, `tokens_used`, `bytes_used`, `truncated`, `section`.
- `SectionCost`: `name`, `returned`, optional `total`, `truncated`. Builders: `new(name, returned)`, `total`, `truncated`.
- `ProvenanceBlock`: ordered `entries: Vec<ProvenanceEntry>` and optional `fingerprint`. Builders: `new`, `entry(label, value)`, `fingerprint`.
- `ProvenanceEntry`: `label`, `value`; `new(label, value)`.

Rendering is crate-private for now and is wired into `AgentResponse` separately. The `budget:` block lists `tokensUsed`, `bytesUsed`, `maxTokens`, `maxBytes`, `maxItems` when set, then `truncated`; the `sections[n]{name,returned,total,truncated}:` roll-up follows only when asked for, and an unknown `total` is a `null` cell. The `provenance:` block lists entries in order, then `fingerprint`. Labels are encoded as TOON keys and values as TOON strings, so newlines and colons in caller text cannot start a line of their own.

### Sections (`section`)

A response can hold several blocks. `AgentResponse::section(Section)` appends one; sections render in insertion order, after the `items()` / `kv_items()` slot when one was set, and before `help[]` and `recovery[]`. The caller owns the order.
